A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdamW/Adam convergence study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support matching retained material against revisions and additions.

before.justification: Figures 1-4 report original training-loss, gradient-norm, parameter-norm and gradient-noise measurements for ResNet50 on CIFAR100 and ImageNet, and GPT-2 on OpenWebText.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a stochastic quadratic optimization experiment in Appendix D, with results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The AdamW moment recursions, decoupled weight decay and parameter update are unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds an explicit GradOracle call for the already assumed stochastic gradient; revised theorem conditions do not introduce a different optimizer.

E1.justification: v2 adds a one-dimensional quadratic optimization scenario with a two-outcome stochastic gradient oracle in Appendix D. The three original image-classification and language-modeling tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: No separate optimizer baseline comparison is added. Figure 5 varies AdamW's weight decay, including its zero-decay special case, as a sensitivity experiment. Comparisons with SGD and other cited optimizers remain theoretical.

E3.justification: The new toy experiment specifies K=10^10, θ=1−1/√K, β=√θ, η=1/√K, ε=10^−10 and six weight-decay settings. The original tasks retain their data splits, batch sizes, training budgets and gradient-logging procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused sensitivity study asking whether large weight decay can prevent convergence even when the minimizer lies inside the constraint. Figure 5 compares averaged gradient norms and iterates for λ from 10^−1 to 10^−5 and zero.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experiments. The new toy trajectories introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All twelve curves in Figures 1-4 and their associated numerical descriptions are retained. Figure 5 newly reports persistent averaged gradients and iterates displaced from x*=5 for λ=10^−1, 10^−2 and 10^−3 in the toy experiment.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces θ≤β≤(1+θ)^2/4 with θ≤β≤√θ; Lemma 2 receives a different proof and changes its bound from 2 to 4. Appendix B corrects 1≤β≤1 to 0≤β≤1, and other proof expressions are repaired. These are contained refinements; the main convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the O(√d/K^(1/4)) gradient-norm guarantee for AdamW, its Adam specialization, and the conditional analogy with SGD's optimal rate. The added norm comparison in the abstract was already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the toy failure as motivation for bounding λ and redirects future work toward loosening that bound. It expands discussion of practical momentum failures and ε's adaptivity tradeoff. Section 2.1 also adds a conditional comparison with an ℓ1 SGD lower bound and explicitly labels the broader optimality extension a conjecture.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release link, specifies the toy objective, stochastic oracle and hyperparameters, and clarifies the different placement of ε in PyTorch's update. Existing deep-learning implementation and hardware details are retained in Appendix E, formerly Appendix D.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Tran et al., Wen et al., Ahn and Cutkosky, Jin et al., and ADOPT. It refines positioning against SGD lower bounds and weakly ε-dependent Adam analyses. Publication updates to already cited works do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained, with localized explanatory expansions and corrections. A new Section 3.3 organizes the existing ε-elimination argument; the conclusion is revised, acknowledgements are added, and experimental details move from Appendix D to E.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into the NeurIPS template, with a narrower text block, redesigned title and author area, removed running headers and reflowed equations. Figures 1-4 are resized and consolidated onto one page, and Figure 5 adds a two-panel display.

improvement.justification: The revised theorem condition and corrected appendix expressions improve mathematical precision. The new weight-decay experiment supports a previously unexplored limitation, while expanded explanations and code-access information improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited: the headline rate and original empirical evidence remain unchanged, and guarantees for standard practical hyperparameters remain unresolved.
